F2-Q1.question: What should we prioritize for the Nov 11 outage?
F2-Q1.answer:
**Priorities for Nov 11: the couch roll DS bearing has no bearing WO, and both refiner plate sets and the reel drum bearing are at risk. Parts are the main gap.**

1. **Couch roll DS bearing: add a WO.**
   - Vibration was 0.072 in/s on the Oct 14 Keel route, rated Good [KV-VR-261014]. It is now 0.243 in/s, above the 0.15 Alert limit, and has been flagged 15 days running [Bonvoy Report 2026-10-31].
   - The only couch roll WO in scope is the seal strip rebuild, WO 26108274, and its parts are not reserved [WO 26108274]. No WO covers the bearing.
   - The daily average rose from 0.138 on Oct 24 to 0.236 on Oct 31 [pi_daily PM1:COUCH_DS_VIB]. That is about 0.014 in/s a day. Extrapolating, it reaches the 0.40 Danger limit around Nov 12, so it may not last to the outage.
   - Ask Keel for an off-route spectrum now, and reserve a bearing.

2. **Reel drum DS bearing, WO 26107420.**
   - This is the outer race defect, now at 0.426 in/s, above the 0.40 Danger limit [Bonvoy Report 2026-10-31].
   - Keel says to change it no later than Nov 11 and to consider a planned stop if it passes 0.50 in/s [KV-VR-261014].
   - The bearing (22238 CCK/W33) is still on order, ETA Nov 5 [WO 26107420]. Action SM-0201 to expedite it is 16 days overdue [Action: Expedite the reel drum DS bearing].

3. **REF 1 and REF 2 plates, WO 26108904 and WO 26108911.**
   - Neither WO has parts reserved. Only one Ridgeway set is on hand for two refiners [Bonvoy Report 2026-10-31].
   - REF 2's set has worn fast since Sep 30, and Ridgeway recommends changing both refiners on Nov 11 [RR-FV-261026]. REF 1 is 72 days into an 84-day life [Bonvoy Report 2026-10-31].
   - Ridgeway quotes a 10-day lead time on a second set [RR-FV-261026]. The order action (SM-0241) was due Oct 28 and is 3 days late [Action: Order a second set of 34" LC refiner plates].
   - Ridgeway suspects sand carry-over from the LC cleaners, so check the reject rates [RR-FV-261026].

4. **2nd section PV fan belts and sheaves, WO 26108281.** Parts are also not reserved [WO 26108281].

5. **Press felts and showers, already reserved.** These are WO 26108953 (2nd press top felt), WO 26109296 (1st press bottom felt) and WO 26108743 (HP shower nozzles) [outage scope].

**Still missing:**
- Parts for four WOs: 26108274, 26108281, 26108904 and 26108911.
- A bearing WO for the couch roll.
- The reel drum bearing delivery.
- The overdue RCFA action to add the shower strainer to every outage clean list [Action: Add the shower strainer to every outage clean list (RCFA-SM-26-024)].

F1-Q1.question: Why did we change the 2nd press top felt early in May?
F1-Q1.answer:
The 2nd press top felt was changed early, on May 19, because it had filled up. The cause was a plugged HP shower, so the felt wasn't being cleaned.

- **Symptoms:** The felt filled at about 3 weeks. Uhle vacuum was up 4.6 inHg, press solids were down 1.8 points, and 4th section steam was at its limit on 34 Super [WO 26105306] [BUS 2026-05-19]. Marlow's analysis put Uhle vacuum at 14.4 inHg on May 18 against about 10 for a felt that age. Press exit solids were 42.1% [MP-FA-260526 p.1].
- **Felt condition:** The felt was 71% filled with stickies, filler and fines, against 40–45% typical. Water content was 1,180 gsm against 780 typical, and air permeability was 9 cfm against 19 [MP-FA-260526 p.1].
- **Root cause:** Spraywell's May 13 audit found 22% of the 2nd press top HP shower nozzles plugged and the supply strainer packed solid. It said the felt "is not being conditioned: expect it to fill" [SW-SA-260513 p.1]. The RCFA gives the same cause [RCFA-SM-26-016].
- **Run and downtime:** The felt ran 34 days against a 42-day target. The change took 7.5 h (450 min) of unplanned downtime [DT-260519-0344].
- **Early warning:** BUS flagged the filling on May 4 [BUS 2026-05-04]. There were also repeated press-area break clusters in late April and May [BUS 2026-05-10] [BUS 2026-05-14].
- **Outcome:** The replacement was running normally, with Uhle vacuum at 9.5 inHg the day before the May 27 outage [MP-SV-260527 p.1].
- **Actions from the RCFA:** The weekly nozzle check [Action: SM-0141] and the outage strainer cleaning [Action: SM-0139] are done. Adding Uhle rate-of-rise to the Bonvoy watch list is late, due July 15 [Action: SM-0138].

H1.question: Overlay Uhle vacuum on the 2nd press top felt for the April felt against the two felts before it, by days on the machine.
H1.answer:
The April felt, installed 2026‑04‑15 and removed 2026‑05‑19 after 33 days, started like the two felts before it. It then filled about 2.5 times faster. All three felts began near 9.3–9.4 inHg. By day 33 the April felt read 14.36 inHg against about 11.05 for each earlier felt.

- **Days 2–12:** The three felts were within about 0.1 inHg of each other, at roughly 9.35 to 9.9 inHg.
- **Day 14 onward:** The April felt pulled away. It was at 11.24 inHg on day 20, against 10.29 and 10.08 for the earlier felts. It was at 13.41 inHg on day 29, against 10.81 on the Jan–Mar felt (day 29) and 10.91 on the Mar–Apr felt (day 30).
- **Rise rate:** I fitted a straight line from the first clean reading to the last. The earlier felts rose about 0.065 inHg/day, from 9.35 to 11.84 over days 2–41 and from 9.39 to 11.91 over days 3–41. The April felt rose about 0.16 inHg/day, from 9.345 on day 2 to 14.36 on day 33.
- **Why it came off early:** The felt record says it was changed early for performance. It lists Uhle vacuum up 4.6 inHg, press solids down 1.8 points, and 4th section steam at its limit on 34 Super [position_life p2-felt-top]. It also says 22% of the HP shower nozzles were plugged (Spraywell audit May 13) [position_life p2-felt-top].
- **Earlier felts:** Both ran the full 41 days and were removed as normal wear. The Mar–Apr felt had some edge filling that was cleaned with the HP shower at mid‑life [position_life p2-felt-top].

The chart uses Pi daily averages for PM1:UHLE_P2T_VAC (day 0 is the install date). I left out days with a stop or outage, where the minimum reading was 0. Those days show as gaps in the lines.

H5.question: Did the May 19 felt change fix the press? Chart the week before against the week after.
H5.answer:
Yes, the press recovered after the May 19 change, on the main press indicators. The change was the 2nd press top felt, installed 2026-05-19 [position_life p2-felt-top]. The old felt was pulled early at 33 days against a 42-day target. It had filled, with Uhle vacuum up 4.6 inHg and press solids down 1.8 points. Its 4th section steam was also at its limit on 34 Super, and 22% of the HP shower nozzles were plugged (Spraywell audit May 13) [position_life p2-felt-top].

Before (May 14–18) against after (May 20–26):
- **Uhle vacuum:** it crept up from 13.41 to 14.36 inHg before the change [Pi PM1:UHLE_P2T_VAC]. After the change it held at about 9.4–9.6 inHg [Pi PM1:UHLE_P2T_VAC].
- **Press exit solids:** about 42.1–42.7% before the change [Pi PM1:PRESS_SOLIDS]. After it, about 44.0–44.2% [Pi PM1:PRESS_SOLIDS]. That is roughly +1.8 points.
- **4th section steam:** the daily average fell from 122–132 psig to 109–128 psig [Pi PM1:DRY4_STEAM_P]. It was still climbing back by May 25–26.
- **Sheet breaks:** 15 in the five clean days before (3.0 per day) against 5 in the seven days after (0.7 per day) [production].
- **Tons per day:** about 687 before (May 14–18) against about 729 after [production].

Two caveats:
- The grade mix changed. 34 Super was 33% of run hours before and 26% after, and 24# went from 40% to 59% [grade_hours]. Some of the break and tonnage gain may be grade mix, not the felt.
- The Uhle and 4th section steam daily averages for May 12–13 and 19 include shutdown periods, so I left those Uhle days blank in the chart.

The plugged HP shower nozzles from the May 13 audit were not shown as fixed in what I pulled. They could shorten this felt's life too.

H2.question: Chart REF 1 against REF 2 specific energy since the Sep 30 outage. At this rate, where will REF 2 be on Nov 11?
H2.answer:
If REF 2 keeps climbing at the current rate, it will be at about 92 kWh/t on Nov 11. That is an extrapolation, not a forecast.

- **REF 2 now:** it averaged 81.3 kWh/t on Oct 31 [pi_daily PM1:REF_B_SE]. It sat near 58 kWh/t through Oct 8, then began rising on Oct 9 (60.5) [pi_daily PM1:REF_B_SE].
- **Rate:** about 1.0 kWh/t per day. That is 60.5 to 81.3 over Oct 9–31 (about 0.95/day), and 70.1 to 81.3 over Oct 20–31 (about 1.0/day) [pi_daily PM1:REF_B_SE]. Adding 11 days to 81.3 gives roughly 92 kWh/t.
- **REF 1:** it is flat at about 60–62 kWh/t, and 62.8 on Oct 31 [pi_daily PM1:REF_A_SE]. The REF 2 rise is therefore not a machine-wide change.
- **Plates:** the new REF 2 set went in on Sep 30 and is only 30 days into an 84-day target [position_life ref-refb]. The previous set was 85% worn at 12 weeks, against a normal of about 60% [position_life ref-refb].
- **BUS:** today's sheet flags REF 2 specific energy "climbing fast on the new plates". It says both refiners are due Nov 11, with one plate set on hand and another to order [BUS 2026-10-31].

H3.question: Did the 3rd section syphon differential warn us before each rotary joint leak? Show the 10 days before each one.
H3.answer:
Partly. The differential warned before two of the three leaks (January and June). It gave almost no usable warning before October. All three leaks were on the DS rotary joint: [WO 26102009] on 2026-01-06, [WO 26106237] on 2026-06-23 and [WO 26108638] on 2026-10-02. The chart shows the 10 days before each one.

- **2026-01-06:** The daily average fell from about 4.3 to 3.3 psi on 12-30 [pi_daily PM1:DRY3_DP]. Bonvoy flagged it low on 01-04, 01-05 and 01-06, which is 2 days of warning. The 01-05 flag was 13 hours outside the band [Bonvoy PM1:DRY3_DP 2026-01-05]. The 12-30 to 01-02 dips are muddied by other stops. The feed shows a vacuum pump failure on 12-31 and a 2nd section syphon failure on 01-01 [downtime_events DT-251230-0089, DT-251231-0091].
- **2026-06-23:** This was the clearest warning. The average slid from about 4.3 psi on 06-18 to 2.5 on 06-21. Bonvoy flagged it low on 06-20, 06-21, 06-22 and 06-23, so about 3 days of warning. The longest flag was 18 hours on 06-21 [Bonvoy PM1:DRY3_DP 2026-06-21].
- **2026-10-02:** The average was 3.6 to 4.1 psi through 09-29, with no sustained fall. The 09-30 dip to 0.86 is the planned outage day. Bonvoy's first flag was 10-01, one day before the leak, at 11 hours low [Bonvoy PM1:DRY3_DP 2026-10-01]. There was also a 3-hour flag on 09-21, 11 days before the leak [Bonvoy PM1:DRY3_DP 2026-09-21]. That one is too early and too short to count as a warning.

So the signal is usually only 1 to 3 days ahead, not 10. Even then, it isn't specific to a joint leak: a falling differential is also what a failing syphon shows. Action SM-0230, a root cause review of the three leaks, is not started and is due 2026-11-20 [Action: SM-0230].

F5-Q1.question: Which repeat failures don't have an RCFA?
F5-Q1.answer:
One repeat failure has no RCFA: the **3rd section rotary joint (DS)**. This covers 2025-11-01 to 2026-10-31. It had 3 unplanned stops totalling 8 h. All three were "Rotary joint leak" and each was fixed by changing the seal kit. [WO 26102009] [WO 26106237] [WO 26108638]

- The stops were on 2026-01-06, 2026-06-23 and 2026-10-02, at about 2.7 h, 2.9 h and 2.4 h. [BUS 2026-01-08] [BUS 2026-06-25] [BUS 2026-10-04]
- A review action exists, "Root cause review: 3rd section rotary joint leaks (Jan, Jun, Oct)". It notes that none of the stops hit the RCFA threshold. It is not started and due 2026-11-20. [Action: SM-0230]

The other eight repeat-stop equipment groups in that period each have at least one RCFA. Those are:
- the dryer drive lineup
- the pulper rotor
- the 2nd press drive
- the 1st press bottom felt
- the 1st press top felt HP shower
- the 2nd press bottom felt
- the headbox
- the 4th section rotary joint (DS)

I checked only whether an RCFA exists, not whether its actions were completed.

H4.question: Is the reel drum bearing temperature following the vibration? Plot both since mid-July.
H4.answer:
Yes. Bearing temperature has risen steadily with vibration since mid-July, and neither has levelled off. I plotted daily maxima, one point every third day. Maxima avoid the low readings on outage and downtime days.

- **Vibration:** The daily average was 0.059 in/s on Jul 15 and 0.426 in/s on Oct 31, about 7 times higher (Pi daily PM1:REEL_DRUM_DS_VIB). It started climbing around Jul 21–23.
- **Temperature:** The daily average went from 134.2°F on Jul 15 to 168.0°F on Oct 31, a rise of about 34°F (Pi daily PM1:REEL_DRUM_DS_TEMP). It began rising at the same time, around Jul 23.
- **Alarm limit:** Vibration is above the 0.4 in/s Danger limit, at 0.426 in/s [Bonvoy Report 2026-10-31]. By my reading of the daily data, it first crossed that limit around Oct 19.
- **Known defect:** Bonvoy notes a known bearing defect, found on the Aug 12 vibration route. It also says Bonvoy doesn't flag this tag because its baseline has moved up with the vibration [Bonvoy Report 2026-10-31].

The two track each other closely, which points to a real bearing problem and not a sensor drift. I found no temperature alarm limit in the data, so I can't say how close the temperature is to one.

P1.question: If the reel drum bearing keeps rising, will it hit Danger before Nov 11?
P1.answer:
**It already has.** The reel drum DS bearing passed the 0.40 in/s Danger limit around Oct 22–23, so the question now is whether it reaches 0.50 before Nov 11. On the current trend it doesn't.

- **Limits:** Keel's limits are Alert 0.15 and Danger 0.40 in/s [KV-VR-251112]. The Bonvoy watch list shows 0.426 in/s (Danger) [Bonvoy Report 2026-10-31]. Bonvoy isn't flagging it because its baseline has moved up with the bearing [Bonvoy Report 2026-10-31].
- **Crossing:** The daily average was 0.4001 on Oct 22, with a max of 0.411 [pi_daily PM1:REEL_DRUM_DS_VIB 2026-10-22]. Oct 31 averaged 0.4259, with a max of 0.431 [pi_daily PM1:REEL_DRUM_DS_VIB 2026-10-31].
- **Projection (extrapolation):** The daily average rose from 0.3907 on Oct 17 to 0.4259 on Oct 31, about 0.0025 in/s per day. At that rate it reaches about 0.45 by Nov 11. It would reach 0.50 only in about 30 days. A faster rise would change this.
- **Keel's trigger:** Keel said to change the bearing no later than the Nov 11 outage, and to consider a planned stop if it passes 0.50 in/s [KV-VR-261014]. Keel's last route, on Oct 14, read 0.39 in/s [KV-VR-261014].

**Parts risk:**
- WO 26107420 (change the bearing, 22238 CCK/W33) is rescheduled for Nov 11 and is "Waiting on parts" [WO 26107420].
- The bearing is on order with an ETA of Nov 5 [WO 26107420]. If that slips, there is no fallback before Nov 11.

I'd confirm the Nov 5 delivery now. I'd also ask Keel for an off-route spectrum reading, because the bearing is already above Danger.

S1.question: Do we break more on 24# than on 34 Super? Chart it.
S1.answer:
Yes, but only modestly. 24# breaks about 35% more often per run hour than 34 Super, though it has about four times as many raw breaks.

- **24#:** 395 breaks in 5,596 h, which is 7.06 per 100 h. [downtime_summary, break events] [grade_hours]
- **34 Super:** 101 breaks in 1,932 h, which is 5.23 per 100 h. [downtime_summary, break events] [grade_hours]
- **Other grades:** 31# is 5.88 per 100 h (57 breaks in 970 h). 28# is 6.72 per 100 h (16 breaks in 238 h, a small sample). [downtime_summary] [grade_hours]

The raw counts mislead because 24# ran 64% of the hours and 34 Super ran 22%. [grade_hours]

By my own rough Poisson check, the gap between 24# and 34 Super is about 2.7 standard errors. That is probably real, not noise, but I haven't tested it formally.

Break time per event is about the same on both grades, at 0.78 h for 24# and 0.77 h for 34 Super. [downtime_summary] The extra loss on 24# therefore comes from frequency, not longer recoveries.

I used 2025-11-01 to 2026-10-31 for the window.

S2.question: Is one crew breaking more than the others? Show it on a chart.
S2.answer:
No. Crew B has the most breaks over 12 months, but the gap is too small to blame B, and it disappears over the last 6 months.

- **Last 12 months:** B had 161 breaks, C 146, D 140 and A 122 [downtime_summary, crew, breaks]. An equal share would be about 142 each (569 ÷ 4). B is 19 above that and A is 20 below. Normal count-to-count scatter at this level is roughly ±12, so both are within about 1.6 to 1.7 times that.
- **Last 6 months (May–Oct):** D had 85, B 82, A 77 and C 73 [downtime_summary, crew, breaks]. The spread is only 12 breaks, which is within normal variation.
- **Break length:** the average break lasts 0.71–0.80 h for every crew over 12 months, so no crew is slower to recover [downtime_summary, crew, breaks].
- **Unplanned stops (not breaks):** D had 12 events and 57.5 h, B had 11 and 49.5 h, A had 11 and 35.9 h, and C had 8 and 33 h over 12 months [downtime_summary, crew, unplanned]. D's total is higher, but the counts are small.

I couldn't normalise by hours run per crew, because the tools only give run hours by grade. I assumed the crews run equal hours. If one crew ran more 24# or other light-grade time, that would change the comparison. I can check the grade mix next if you want.

S3.question: Make a monthly chart of tons and break hours. Which month hurt most, and why?
S3.answer:
May hurt most. It had the most breaks and break hours of any month, and the lowest tons per day. The chart is above.

- **May:** 73 breaks and 52.2 break hours, against 37–56 breaks in every other month [Production 2026-05]. Output was 20,316 t, which is 655 t/day, the lowest daily rate of the year [Production 2026-05]. Uptime was 94.1% [Production 2026-05].
- **Other months:** July is next worst at 42–45 break hours and 93.5% uptime. February has the lowest monthly total, 19,579 t, but only because it has 28 days [Production 2026-07, 2026-02].

Why May was bad:
- **Press section:** It caused 24 breaks, 28.8 h, which is 55% of break time [downtime_summary 2026-05]. It also caused 4 of the 5 unplanned stops, 18.7 h [downtime_summary 2026-05].
- **Press felt problems:** Felts plugged on the 2nd press bottom (321 min, 12 May) and the 1st press bottom (217 min, 13 May) [DT-260512-0322, DT-260513-0327].
  - The Uhle vacuum had been climbing and press solids falling for 16 and 26 days before those stops. Nothing acted on those trends [DT-260512-0322, DT-260513-0327].
- **Other press stops:** The 2nd press top felt was changed early at 3 weeks (450 min, 19 May), with Uhle vacuum up 4.6 inHg and 4th section steam at its limit [DT-260519-0344]. A 1st press bottom felt blew on 3 May (135 min) [DT-260503-0289].
- **Hood exhaust fan:** It failed on 28 May (307 min). Hood exhaust temperature and moisture had been drifting for 23 days [DT-260528-0354].
- **RCFAs:** RCFA-SM-26-014 to -017 were raised for these stops [DT-260512-0322, DT-260513-0327, DT-260519-0344, DT-260528-0354].
- **Grade:** 24# was 69% of run hours, so grade mix doesn't explain it [grade_hours 2026-05].

The downtime feed shows slightly different break hours for some months, for example 42.6 h for July against 44.6 h in production. I charted the production figures.

P2.question: When was the calender bottom roll last ground?

PM1 has no calender, so there is no calender bottom roll to have been ground. The roll list, the dryer and press drawings, and the work orders, BUS issues and actions contain no calender position or grinding record. A search of the records for "calender" returned nothing.

The nearest match is the 2nd press bottom roll, if that is what you meant. Pellham Roll Service reground it to spec crown after it came off the machine on 09/30/2026, and the report is dated 10/09/2026 [DOC PR-RS-261009-p2bottom p.1]. The shop took 0.11 in off the diameter and replaced the bearings. The roll went back to stores as the spare [DOC PR-RS-261009-p2bottom p.1].

If you meant a different roll, tell me which position and I'll check its history.
